transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I came in because I just don’t feel like myself anymore. Most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of this dark hole, and I can see people up above me going about their lives, talking, laughing, doing normal things, but I can’t get myself up there with them.

Even when I’m around people I know, people I should feel comfortable with, there’s this heaviness that just sits on me. It’s like a hopeless feeling I can’t shake off, no matter what I tell myself. I kept thinking maybe it would pass, or maybe I was just having a rough stretch, but it’s been bad enough that I finally thought… I need to talk to someone, because I don’t really know how to get out of it on my own.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… about a year and two months now, I think. It really started after that fall I had on the HVAC job last fall, when I hurt my back. Before that I had bad days like anybody, but after the injury, everything just started kind of unraveling, one thing after another, and I never really got back to feeling like myself. 

At first I kept telling myself it was temporary, like once I healed up or things settled down, I’d be okay again. But the weeks kept turning into months, and now it’s been over a year, and I’m still in this place.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy before you started feeling this way?

No… not really. That’s actually one of the things that scares me, because I used to have things that made me feel like me. I used to love hiking, even just getting out on a trail and noticing the little things, like the way the light came through the trees or how quiet everything got once you were far enough in. And I painted, not anything fancy, but I liked having colors out and getting lost in it for a while.

I also used to go to the makerspace and tinker with stuff, fix little things, mess around with tools, try to figure out how something could be put together better. Even at work, I used to get a kind of satisfaction from a tricky install, like when something was a pain and nobody could quite figure it out, and then I’d finally get it working. That used to feel good.

Now I’ll look at my paint supplies and just… stare at them. Or I’ll think about going to the makerspace and I can’t make myself move. People will call or text about going on a hike or working on something, and I’ll ignore it because it feels like too much, or like there’s no point. It’s not that I suddenly hate those things. It’s more like the part of me that cared about starting them just isn’t there.
Have you ever thought about ending your life during this difficult time?

Yeah… I have. I don’t really like saying that out loud, but yes.

It’s not every second of the day, but there have been times where I lie there and think… maybe everyone would just be better off if I didn’t wake up. Like I’m just this weight people have to keep carrying. And when the pain gets bad and then the money stuff starts piling up in my head, it can get really dark really fast. Sometimes I catch myself thinking about ending it, and then that scares me, because part of me doesn’t want to be thinking that way. It’s like I don’t want to die exactly, I just don’t know how to keep going like this.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see during this difficult time?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m so exhausted or upset that my mind kind of runs away with me, and I’ll get stuck in my own thoughts, but I haven’t heard voices like someone talking to me when no one’s there.

And I haven’t seen things, like… people or shapes or anything that other people couldn’t see. Sometimes at night I might misread a shadow or think I heard the house settling and get startled, but then I can tell what it is. It’s not like something is actually there.

So, no, not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before you started feeling this way?

Yes… definitely. Everything feels slowed down now. Like even simple things take me so much longer than they should.

I’ll be sitting on the couch and think, okay, get up and go to the kitchen, and it’s like my body doesn’t respond right away. I’m not even doing anything complicated, just standing up, walking across the room, getting a glass of water or something, but it feels like I’m moving through water. Heavy, slow… like there’s a delay between deciding to move and actually doing it.

And people notice it. They’ll ask me, “Are you okay?” or they’ll look at me like something’s wrong because I guess I’m moving slower or taking too long to answer. Even answering a simple question can feel like my brain has to drag the words up from somewhere. I know what they asked me, but it takes me a while to respond, and then I feel embarrassed because I can tell there’s this pause that shouldn’t be there.

Before, I was always moving around for work, fixing things, getting tools, figuring stuff out. I wasn’t like this. Now everything feels like it takes a ridiculous amount of effort, and I hate that people can see it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?

Yeah… I think so, but I haven’t been keeping track the way I probably should. My clothes fit different some days, and I know my eating has gotten really messed up.

It’s like… during the day, I’ll just run on coffee. I’ll tell myself I’m going to eat something, but then when I actually look at food, it kind of turns my stomach. Not always like I’m going to throw up, just… nothing sounds good, and the idea of chewing and swallowing feels like too much. So I’ll go hours and hours without really eating anything, and then I realize it’s late and I’ve barely had more than coffee.

But then at night, it flips in this weird way. I’ll be standing in the kitchen, opening cabinets, picking at crackers or cereal or whatever’s there, not because I’m hungry exactly. It’s more like I’m just trying to put something in me, or I don’t even know what I’m doing. I don’t really taste it. I’ll eat a few bites of something, then leave it, then come back again later.

So yeah, my appetite is all over the place. I don’t have normal meals like I used to. It feels like my body doesn’t know what it wants anymore.
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still lately?

Not really restless, no… it’s more the opposite, honestly. I’m not pacing around or feeling like I can’t sit still. I sit still too much, if anything.

Everything I do is slow now. Like, I’ll be on the couch and know I need to get up and go to the kitchen, and it feels like this whole process just to make my body do it. I’ll sit there thinking, “Okay, get up,” and then there’s this delay, like I’m moving through thick water or something. Even walking across the room feels heavier than it should.

And it’s not just moving around. If someone asks me a simple question, I can hear them, I understand it, but answering takes me longer. The words don’t come out right away. People keep asking me if I’m okay because I guess I look slowed down, or I’m taking too long to respond. It makes me feel really self-conscious, because I know I’m not acting like myself.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled by someone or something else?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, my thoughts feel awful and heavy sometimes, but they still feel like mine, if that makes sense.

I don’t feel like someone else is putting thoughts in my head or controlling them. It’s more like I get stuck in my own head, but not like there’s another person or force doing it. I haven’t had anything where I thought someone was steering my mind or making me think things against my will.
Have you had periods where your depressive symptoms significantly improved for at least a couple of months at a time since you first started feeling this way?

No… not really. I wish I could say there was a stretch like that, but I don’t think there has been.

This has been going on for about a year and two months now, since that fall at the HVAC job when I hurt my back, and after that it just felt like everything started unraveling. There might be a day here or there where I’m a little more functional, or I can get through something I have to do, but it hasn’t been like, “Oh, I’m better now,” for a couple months at a time. Not even close.

It’s been more like this long, dragging thing that started back then and just… stayed.
Have you had any periods, even brief ones, where you felt completely back to your normal self since this all started?

No… I don’t think I’ve had any period where I felt completely back to myself, even for a short time.

It’s been going on about a year and two months now, ever since I fell at the HVAC job and hurt my back, and after that everything just kind of started unraveling. I keep thinking maybe I’ll wake up one day and feel like the old me again, even just for a little while, but it hasn’t really happened like that. There are moments where I can get through something or look more “normal” from the outside, I guess, but inside it still feels like I’m carrying all of it. So no, not completely back to normal.
Have you had two or more months in a row since this started where you felt consistently depressed most of the day?

Yes… definitely. I mean, that’s honestly why I came in. Most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of this dark hole, and it’s not just for a few minutes here and there. It hangs over me most of the day.

Even if I’m around people I know, or I’m trying to act normal, I still can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It’s like it follows me around, and I can be in the same room with other people and still feel completely weighed down by it. So yes, it’s been more than two months in a row where I’ve felt depressed most of the day.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you didn't feel depressed at all?

No… I really don’t think so. I can’t remember any two-week stretch where I just didn’t feel depressed at all.

That’s part of why I came in, honestly. Most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of this dark hole, and even if I’m around people I know, or I’m trying to seem okay, I can’t shake that heavy, hopeless feeling. Maybe there have been hours where I’m distracted or I’m functioning better, but not two whole weeks where it’s gone. Not where I’d say, “I’m not depressed anymore.”
Have you had more than one period of significant depression in your life, before this current episode started?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean… I’ve had hard times before in my life, sure, times where I was down or stressed or felt overwhelmed, but I don’t know if I’d call them “significant depression” the way this has been.

This current thing feels different to me, like it settled in and didn’t let up. Before this, I don’t remember having separate episodes like this where I would say, yes, that was another period of major depression. But I also don’t want to say my memory is perfect, because when you’re trying to think back over years, it all gets kind of blurry. I guess I’d say I can’t really identify more than one clear period like this before now.
Have you experienced any significant differences between this current episode of depression and any previous episodes you may have had?

I’m not sure I can really compare them, because I don’t have a clear picture of previous episodes like this. I’ve had rough periods before, like I said, but this is the one that stands out as… this ongoing thing that I can actually point to.

So I don’t know if I’d say there are “differences” exactly, because I’m not even fully sure those earlier times count the same way. They feel blurry when I try to line them up in my head. This current one just feels more definite to me, like it’s been much harder to shake and more clearly present day after day.

But if you mean, like, “was there another time that was similar but had different features,” I don’t think I can say that for sure. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m giving you a clean before-and-after comparison when I really don’t have one.
Have you had any periods of depression like this before the one that started after your injury?

I don’t really know. I mean, before the injury, I had times where I was unhappy or worn down or just not myself, but I can’t honestly point to a period and say, yes, that was like this.

This feels tied together in my mind with what happened after the injury, like that’s when it became something I couldn’t just push through or explain away as a bad stretch. Before that, there were rough times, but they’re kind of vague when I try to think back. I don’t want to say “no, never” like I’m absolutely certain, because memory gets messy, but I also can’t give you a clear example of depression like this before then.
Have you had two or more episodes of depression in your lifetime that lasted for at least two weeks?

I don’t think I can say yes to that. I mean, I understand what you’re asking — like, have there been two separate stretches in my life where I was depressed for at least a couple weeks — but when I look back, I can’t clearly identify two like that.

There have definitely been times where I was down or going through something hard, and maybe some of those lasted a while, but I don’t know that they were the same as this or that I’d count them as separate episodes. It’s hard because when you’re living your life, you don’t always mark it off like, “Okay, this was two weeks, this was an episode.” It all sort of blends together looking back.

So… I guess my honest answer is I’m not sure, but I don’t have two clear episodes I can point to. This current one is the one that feels clear to me.
Have you had any episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks before the one that started after your injury?

I know you’re trying to pin down whether there was something clearly before the injury, and I’m sorry, I just don’t have a clean answer for that.

Before then, I had periods where I felt low or stressed or like I was dragging myself through things, but I can’t honestly look back and say, “That was definitely an episode that lasted at least two weeks.” I didn’t track it that way, and it’s all kind of mixed in with normal life problems in my memory.

So I guess the most truthful answer is: I’m not sure. I don’t have a specific earlier two-week period of depression that I can point to with confidence. This one after the injury is the one that feels clear and definite to me.
Have you noticed that your depressive episodes tend to occur at a specific time of the year?

I can’t say I’ve noticed a pattern like that, no. I mean, I’ve thought about it a little, because I know some people get worse in winter or around certain seasons, but for me it doesn’t really stand out that way.

It feels more connected to what was going on in my life and everything after the injury than to, like, the month or the weather or the holidays or anything seasonal. I’m not saying it’s impossible there’s some pattern I’ve missed, but I haven’t been able to look back and say, “Oh, this always happens in the fall,” or “Every winter it gets bad.” It hasn’t been that clear for me.

target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year and two months, ever since the fall at the HVAC job left me with the back injury and everything started unraveling.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether there have been any symptom-free or normal periods since the depressive episode began, which is most directly about the duration and continuity of the symptoms.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think I’ve had any period where I felt completely back to myself, even for a short time.

It’s been going on about a year and two months now, ever since I fell at the HVAC job and hurt my back, and after that everything just kind of started unraveling. I keep thinking maybe I’ll wake up one day and feel like the old me again, even just for a little while, but it hasn’t really happened like that. There are moments where I can get through something or look more “normal” from the outside, I guess, but inside it still feels like I’m carrying all of it. So no, not completely back to normal.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of a major depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you had two or more months in a row since this started where you felt consistently depressed most of the day?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because most days I feel like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole, and even when I’m around people I know, I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about sustained depressed mood most of the day over a period of two or more months.

patient.answer:
Yes… definitely. I mean, that’s honestly why I came in. Most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of this dark hole, and it’s not just for a few minutes here and there. It hangs over me most of the day.

Even if I’m around people I know, or I’m trying to act normal, I still can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It’s like it follows me around, and I can be in the same room with other people and still feel completely weighed down by it. So yes, it’s been more than two months in a row where I’ve felt depressed most of the day.

doctor.intent: determine if there are any distinct episodes of depression
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you didn't feel depressed at all?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: I came in because most days I feel like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole, and even when I’m around people I know, I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether there has been any two-week period without feeling depressed, which directly concerns the presence or absence of depressed mood over time.

patient.answer:
No… I really don’t think so. I can’t remember any two-week stretch where I just didn’t feel depressed at all.

That’s part of why I came in, honestly. Most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of this dark hole, and even if I’m around people I know, or I’m trying to seem okay, I can’t shake that heavy, hopeless feeling. Maybe there have been hours where I’m distracted or I’m functioning better, but not two whole weeks where it’s gone. Not where I’d say, “I’m not depressed anymore.”

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean… I’ve had hard times before in my life, sure, times where I was down or stressed or felt overwhelmed, but I don’t know if I’d call them “significant depression” the way this has been.

This current thing feels different to me, like it settled in and didn’t let up. Before this, I don’t remember having separate episodes like this where I would say, yes, that was another period of major depression. But I also don’t want to say my memory is perfect, because when you’re trying to think back over years, it all gets kind of blurry. I guess I’d say I can’t really identify more than one clear period like this before now.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can really compare them, because I don’t have a clear picture of previous episodes like this. I’ve had rough periods before, like I said, but this is the one that stands out as… this ongoing thing that I can actually point to.

So I don’t know if I’d say there are “differences” exactly, because I’m not even fully sure those earlier times count the same way. They feel blurry when I try to line them up in my head. This current one just feels more definite to me, like it’s been much harder to shake and more clearly present day after day.

But if you mean, like, “was there another time that was similar but had different features,” I don’t think I can say that for sure. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m giving you a clean before-and-after comparison when I really don’t have one.

patient.answer:
I don’t really know. I mean, before the injury, I had times where I was unhappy or worn down or just not myself, but I can’t honestly point to a period and say, yes, that was like this.

This feels tied together in my mind with what happened after the injury, like that’s when it became something I couldn’t just push through or explain away as a bad stretch. Before that, there were rough times, but they’re kind of vague when I try to think back. patient.answer:
I don’t think I can say yes to that. I mean, I understand what you’re asking — like, have there been two separate stretches in my life where I was depressed for at least a couple weeks — but when I look back, I can’t clearly identify two like that.

There have definitely been times where I was down or going through something hard, and maybe some of those lasted a while, but I don’t know that they were the same as this or that I’d count them as separate episodes. It’s hard because when you’re living your life, you don’t always mark it off like, “Okay, this was two weeks, this was an episode.” It all sort of blends together looking back.

So… I guess my honest answer is I’m not sure, but I don’t have two clear episodes I can point to. This current one is the one that feels clear to me.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's depressive episodes are recurrent
doctor.question: Have you had any episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks before the one that started after your injury?

patient.answer:
I know you’re trying to pin down whether there was something clearly before the injury, and I’m sorry, I just don’t have a clean answer for that.

Before then, I had periods where I felt low or stressed or like I was dragging myself through things, but I can’t honestly look back and say, “That was definitely an episode that lasted at least two weeks.” I didn’t track it that way, and it’s all kind of mixed in with normal life problems in my memory.

So I guess the most truthful answer is: I’m not sure. I don’t have a specific earlier two-week period of depression that I can point to with confidence. This one after the injury is the one that feels clear and definite to me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's depressive episodes have a seasonal pattern

patient.answer:
I can’t say I’ve noticed a pattern like that, no. I mean, I’ve thought about it a little, because I know some people get worse in winter or around certain seasons, but for me it doesn’t really stand out that way.

It feels more connected to what was going on in my life and everything after the injury than to, like, the month or the weather or the holidays or anything seasonal. I’m not saying it’s impossible there’s some pattern I’ve missed, but I haven’t been able to look back and say, “Oh, this always happens in the fall,” or “Every winter it gets bad.” It hasn’t been that clear for me.
